readings.title: Tone I: resurrection hymn
readings.text: While the stone was sealed by the Jews, and soldiers stood on guard over thy body undefiled, thou didst rise on the third day, O Saviour, who givest life unto the world. For which cause the Heavenly Powers cried aloud unto thee, O Giver of Life: Glory to thy resurrection, O Christ! Glory to thy kingdom! Glory to thy providence, O thou who alone lovest mankind!

readings.title: Tone VIII: resurrection hymn
readings.text: Thou didst descend from on high, O Tender-hearted One; thou didst endure the three-days' burial, that thou mightest free us from our passions, O our Life and Resurrection. Glory, O Lord, to thee.

scripture.text: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

overview.text: The texts sung in worship also express Christian teaching. The two resurrection hymns here proclaim Christ’s rising and saving work, while their tone labels connect the words with the Church’s musical traditions.

readings.title: What does the Tone I resurrection hymn proclaim?

paragraphs.text: The hymn contrasts the sealed tomb and soldiers’ guard with Christ’s resurrection on the third day. Its praise identifies him as the giver of life and connects resurrection with his kingdom and care for humanity.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What does the Tone VIII hymn proclaim?

paragraphs.text: This hymn connects Christ’s descent, burial and resurrection with deliverance from the passions. Passions here means disordered impulses from which the hymn speaks of liberation. The words express doctrine in a compact sung form.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What does the tones tutorial contain?

paragraphs.text: The OCA tutorial introduces eight tones through musical phrases and examples in Common Obikhod and Kievan chant. It includes written explanations and recorded demonstrations, identifying particular musical traditions rather than presenting every Orthodox chant practice as identical.
